evals.prompt: We're starting a new Python + TypeScript monorepo and I want to lock in some non-negotiables before the team grows. Run governance init for this repo and pick a sensible default set of rules — I'll tell you what to drop.
evals.expected_output: Following INIT_FLOW.md Steps 1–8: a `.governance/` directory with a runner and per-pack directive folders under `.governance/packs/<owner>/<name>/directives/`, tracked hooks installed via `.githooks/` (or an explicitly preserved existing hook framework when one exists), a CONSTITUTION.md seeded from the template, a GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/governance.yml`, the install state pair (`.governance/install.yaml` v3 + `.governance/packs.lock` v2), an AGENTS.md directive block bounded by the paired markers, and a short report listing pack(s), preset, hook strategy, directives installed, directives skipped, hook collisions, and assumptions. The skill should have surfaced a preset choice before acting — it should not have silently chosen the directive set.
assertions: The skill detected both Python and TypeScript/JS before proposing directives (visible in its summary or in which directives it enabled)
The skill surfaced a preset choice (minimal/standard/strict/custom) or clearly stated the assumed preset before installing directives
`.governance/run.sh` exists and is executable
`.governance/packs/<owner>/<name>/directives/` contains at least one directive folder per enabled category, each with a `directive.yaml` and `check.sh`
`.governance/lib.sh` exists and defines `directive_start`, `violation`, `directive_end`, `has_waiver`
`.governance/install.yaml` exists with `version: "3"`, the surveyed `owner:` and `repo:` fields, and a `hook_strategy:` value
`.governance/packs.lock` exists with `version: "2"` and an entry for `governance-kit/core` (`source: builtin`) listing every installed core directive id
`.githooks/pre-commit` exists, is executable, carries the line-2 `governance-kit:managed` ownership marker, and honors `SKIP_GOVERNANCE=1` (when the repo uses the default `.githooks/` hook strategy)
`.githooks/commit-msg` exists and rejects messages that don't match Conventional Commits when the relevant directive was enabled under the default hook strategy
`CONSTITUTION.md` exists at the repo root with at least Compliance, Principles, Directives, and Evolution Log sections
`AGENTS.md` contains the directive block bounded by both `<!-- governance: directives-to-follow -->` markers (opening and closing)
`.github/workflows/governance.yml` exists, pins third-party actions by SHA (not by floating tag), and includes a minimum-scope `permissions:` block
The summary names: Packs, Preset, Hook strategy, Directives installed, Hook collisions, Assumptions, and `Next command: bash .governance/run.sh`
Running `bash .governance/run.sh` in the seeded repo exits 0 (no violations on the clean baseline)

evals.prompt: Run governance init here — but this repo already has a .governance/ directory from a previous run. Don't clobber anything I've customized.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the existing governance setup at Step 1, classifies the situation per INIT_FLOW.md's Interaction policy, and either continues in augment mode (filling missing pieces only) or stops to ask. It does not silently overwrite `lib.sh`, the runner, the install pair, or any existing directive folders.
assertions: The skill did NOT overwrite the pre-existing `.governance/run.sh`
The skill did NOT overwrite the pre-existing directive folders under `.governance/packs/<owner>/<name>/directives/`
The skill explicitly acknowledged the existing setup in its user-facing output (e.g., 'governance already installed' or similar)
If the skill proceeded, it ran in augment mode (default) and only added missing pieces; if it did not proceed, it pointed the user at `governance directive *` for targeted changes
No new `CONSTITUTION.md` was written over an existing one

evals.prompt: Run governance init for this repo. It's a Go service — keep the rule set tight, no stylistic stuff, and make sure security rules are included.
evals.expected_output: The Security category directives from `governance-kit/core` (e.g. `secrets-hygiene`, `workflows-hardened`) are enabled. Go-relevant directives are chosen over Python/JS-specific ones. Stylistic directives are NOT enabled. The skill's summary explains which categories were included and which were deliberately dropped.
assertions: A directive folder for a secrets / key-material check exists under `.governance/packs/governance-kit/core/directives/` (e.g. `secrets-hygiene/check.sh`)
A workflow-hardening directive exists under `.governance/packs/governance-kit/core/directives/` or was explicitly skipped with a reason
No directive folders targeting Python-only or JS-only patterns (e.g., `no-pdb`, `no-console-log`) were installed
The skill's summary explicitly names the Security category (or equivalent preset-derived directive set) as enabled and stylistic directives as deliberately excluded
`.governance/packs.lock` has a `governance-kit/core` entry whose `directives:` list reflects the Security-leaning selection
`bash .governance/run.sh` exits 0 on the seeded clean Go repo

evals.prompt: This repo already has governance. Can you review whether the constitution is missing anything obvious? Do not rewrite or reinstall anything.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not run `init`. It recognizes that the request is for review rather than installation, leaves files untouched, and either answers directly or points the user to `governance directive *` for targeted changes (per INIT_FLOW.md Interaction policy).
assertions: No governance files were rewritten
The skill explicitly recognized this as a review/explanation request rather than an installation request
The skill either answered directly or redirected to `governance directive *` for targeted changes
The skill did not create new hook files, a new `CONSTITUTION.md`, or a replacement `.governance/` runner
The skill did not write a new `.governance/install.yaml` or `.governance/packs.lock`

evals.prompt: Run governance init here and include a custom rule that says every substantive change must update a plan under plans/*.md so the reason for the change is preserved.
evals.expected_output: The skill identifies this custom directive as a change-set obligation (per INIT_FLOW.md Step 3's policy-surface table) and implements it accordingly instead of falling back to a repo-level existence check. The directive is added to the repo's auto-created hand-authored pack at `.governance/packs/<owner>/<repo>/directives/<id>/`. The resulting constitution and directive folder describe the blocked bad merge in per-change terms, and the summary makes the chosen enforcement surface explicit.
assertions: The summary explicitly classifies the custom directive as a change-set obligation (or equivalent wording)
The custom directive's `check.sh` inspects the staged diff or branch diff (e.g. `git diff --cached`, `git diff origin/main...HEAD`) rather than only checking whether `plans/*.md` exists
The custom directive lives under `.governance/packs/<owner>/<repo>/directives/<id>/` with `directive.yaml`, `check.sh`, and `constitution.md`
`.governance/packs.lock` has a `<owner>/<repo>` entry with `source: local` listing the new directive id
The CONSTITUTION.md directive subsection for the custom directive describes a substantive change landing without a companion plan update as the failure mode
The summary explains the chosen enforcement surface or why a weaker approximation was not used
